This is exactly what we were looking for. We use it not only for beverages, but also as an overflow refrigerator. The shelves are removable, which allows you to store larger items when needed (such as a gallon of milk).

We keep the unit in the "mud room", where the ambient temperature is a fairly steady 60 degrees in the Winter (will be closer to 80 degrees in the Summer). I like my drinks cold, so I put it on the "5" setting (two notches below the coldest setting). This keeps it right near 32 degrees. Any colder and the drinks would freeze. I expect that I will need to set it to "7" in the Summer.

Overall, it does the job at the right price; looks nice; and is not a loud unit. The only drawback is that the internal light is manual, not automatic. If you operate the unit in a dark place, I could see it possibly being a slight inconvenience to have to manually the switch the light on and off each time. But in my case, this is not a problem. It is also still too early to tell how much impact this will have on my electric bill.

After a year and a half, my Whynter BR-128WS Beverage Refrigerator began making an extremely loud, reverberating sound and overheating. I turned the fridge off and this continued. I unplugged the device and it finally stopped. This happened a day before I left for vacation. Had it happened one day later, my house likely would have burned down.

Things happen in life and even the best product can have the rare problem. Based on other reviews I've read, this seems to be a rare case. Either that or no one else waited long enough to compose or add to their review. All in all, I loved the fridge. It looks great and worked great, up until it almost burned my house down.
